jobs.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 25% of the Time Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems Long Range Air Defense & Domestic Systems (LRAD & DS) Operating Unit specializes in the development, manufacture, assembly, testing, and sustainment of international Air Surveillance Sensors and Systems, Bio-detection systems, and Air Traffic Control capabilities. This is a worldwide international business with customers in North Africa, Middle East, Southeast Asia and South and Central America.  We are seeking a Program Management Senior Director to join our team of qualified and diverse individuals. This position will be located in Elkridge, MD.

The position has P&L responsibility for management, strategy, and execution including establishing a strong trajectory for growing the business. This position reports to the VP, Land & Maritime Sensors Business Unit. In addition, this position has significant senior leadership contact and will require a candidate with strong leadership and decision-making skills with the ability to perform in an environment of ambiguity and continuous change. The position must role model leadership values and behaviors. The candidate must have strong communication, executive presence, and cross-cultural skills to be able to effectively interact with a geographically disbursed senior leadership team.

Responsibilities include:
- Capture and execution of international contracts through both Direct Commercial Sales (DCS) and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) contractual structures

- Lead and direct cross-functional teams to meet program cost, schedule and technical performance objectives in a matrix organizational environment

- Establish milestones and monitor adherence to master plans and schedules, risk/opportunity management, identifies program problems and obtains solutions
- Identify, allocate and manage program resources, including workforce planning
- Create a positive employee experience for the employees assigned to the operating unit by focusing on retention initiatives and supporting professional development
- Deliver presentations to customers, executive management and other program stakeholders
- Cultivate customer relationships and intimacy to develop further opportunities within the customer community
- Develop business area strategies and new business opportunities that are consistent with Division/ Sector priorities to drive consistent growth for the operating area
- Engage Commission Sales Representatives (CSRs) to assist in the marketing and sale of products to foreign governments, where applicable
- Develop relationships with high-ranking military officials and local Embassy officials in pursuit of new business opportunities
- Develop relationships with senior leaders in partner industries (suppliers, subcontracting) including international companies
- Lead the negotiation of contracts, contract changes, specifications, operating budgets, schedule milestones, and key terms and conditions.
- Proactively identify trends, risks, and opportunities within the organization and develop solutions in partnership with peers, division and matrix leadership, and regional/division HR business leaders
- Using data and analytics, develop solutions to current business issues as well as proactively engage in risk mitigation.
- Analyze and concisely present information to the management team to enable good business decisions

Basic Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree with 15 or more years of program management or related experience; OR Master's degree with 12 or more years of program management or related experience. Minimum 7 years of international program management with DCS contracts in at least two diverse geographical regions.

- Expertise negotiating contracts with international customers including at least one MENA country.

- Experience with US Government FMS contracts
- Experience with US Export Regulations /licensing processes and their applicability to Foreign DCS and FMS contracts
- Expertise in program execution to lead the performance of tasks on schedule and at cost on Development and Production programs
- International Capture and Proposal management experience
- Proven success in leading and influencing individuals and teams in a matrix environment
- Demonstrated ability to foster existing customer relationships and develop new customer relationships
- Strong communication and executive presence skills to effectively interact with customer and senior leadership
- Must be a US citizen with a minimum active US Government Secret Clearance; OR DoE equivalent

Preferred Qualifications:
- Master's degree in engineering and/or business administration

- Experience with International Consultants and CSRs
- Experience developing and implementing offset/localization projects with international companies
- 8 or more years leading production programs, development programs or technical teams (engineering management, functional management)
- Demonstrated knowledge of strategic planning and new business development
- Demonstrated knowledge of radar systems

- Conversational French, Spanish or Arabic
- Understanding of cultural sensitivities by region specifically in MENA region

Primary Level Salary Range: $254,200.00 - $381,200.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

- Experience in affordability, operational efficiency, or build-time acceleration.

This role will report directly to the Operating Unit (OU) Director and act as Chief of Staff for the OU. The ideal candidate thrives on shaping and developing high-value strategy and execution of multiple projects for a complex program, orchestrating proposal activities to achieve organization goals that align with customer’s strategic objectives while ensuring successful program execution.

The position requires a solution-based mindset and the demonstrated ability to develop practical execution plans in a dynamic and complex environment. The selected candidate must demonstrate a proven track record of solving complex problems through systematic and objective evaluation of information and data resulting in effective communication, collaboration, and implementation of a strong operational foundation with a diverse set of internal and external customers and suppliers. This position requires a candidate with strong organizational and decision-making skills with the ability to lead in an environment of continuous change. This position requires the ability to report out at the Executive level, including status, planning, and execution.  Collaboration with programs and functional leaders to develop and nurture a highly competent and engaged team that delivers on commitments and embodies “best culture” is essential.

The successful candidate in this role will be interested/energized by and able to:

- Drive operating rhythms and cadences across the OU, including weekly status reports, executive‑ready communications, and timely follow‑up on actions.
- Plan and facilitate effective staff meetings with focused agendas, calendar reviews, task and risk tracking, and appropriate analytics to support decision‑making.
- Engage with employees and leaders at all levels, from individual contributors to executive leadership, to understand requirements and expectations and help foster a positive, retentive team culture.
- Manage execution across the team, including calendar integration, task tracking, customer engagement coordination, and internal deliverables, ensuring commitments are clear and met.
- Serve as the focal point for communication, planning, and collaboration for internal logistics and integrator activities within the OU.
- Lead regular team and cross‑functional forums to surface issues and concerns, drive alignment, and ensure timely resolution of actions.
- Improve operational efficiency of systems, processes, and practices in support of the OU’s mission, identifying bottlenecks and driving continuous improvement.
- Oversee execution of key strategic projects and deliverables, engaging all relevant stakeholders, establishing needed partnerships, developing program plans, and driving accountability for performance.
- Integrate metrics and develop/refine dashboards, leveraging digital transformation opportunities to streamline procedures, processes, and communication across the OU.
- Prepare OU leadership for meetings and events, including agenda review, data collection and synthesis, and coordination of pre‑briefs and read‑ahead materials.

Our Leaders at Northrop Grumman live our values daily and encourage our teams to do the same. We do the right thing: upholding the highest ethical standards and facilitating a safe and respectful environment that attracts, retains, and inspires a diverse and engaged team. We do what we promise: holding yourself and others accountable to meet predictable and balanced results. We commit to shared success: operating as OneNG and removing barriers for our teams. Finally, We pioneer: setting a vision that shapes the future and inspires others.

Basic Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree and 10 years (or Bachelor of Science in STEM and 9 years) of related experience as defined below, OR a Master’s degree and 8 years (or Master of Science in STEM and 7 years) of related experience as defined below:

The Chief Information and Digital Office (CIDO) Project Management Office for Space Sector plays a critical role in delivering technology and digital solutions across the business. To align work with business priorities and ensure clear accountability, the CIDO Program Manager (PM) function is organized by divisional business unit and solution, enabling teams to focus on the specific needs of each business area while driving consistent, scalable delivery of IT capabilities.

This role provides CIDO leadership to technical teams delivering innovative information technology and security solutions in satisfaction of program requirements.

The CIDO PM works closely with other Functions and Shared Services teams, including Classified Solutions, Facilities, Physical Security, InfoSec/Cyber Security, Infrastructure Services, IT Operations, and Application Services, to securely deploy, maintain, and optimize IT services that enable enterprise classified and unclassified operations. The CIDO PM leads key activities including IT governance (chairing infrastructure design reviews and change boards), cost account management (financial budgeting and performance management), business continuity planning (developing and testing information systems continuity plans), proposal development (IT solutions design and pricing for new IT statements of work), and crisis management planning and incident recovery.

(MEP) is a leading designer, producer, and supplier of spacecraft components that power and enable satellites of all classes. Northrop Grumman Defense Systems (DS) is seeking a Weapons Aircraft Integration Program Manager 3 for the Advanced Weapons Business Unit located in Northridge, CA. Our Advanced Weapons team designs, develops, manufactures and integrates missile systems that support U.S. national and allied security objectives.

This position is required to be full-time, on-site in the Northridge, CA location. No remote/telework arrangement is available for this position. Applicants must have a current U.S. Government DoW Secret clearance with ability to get a Sensitive Access Program (SAP) clearance .

DESCRIPTION:
The Weapons Integration Program Manager 3 will own end‑to‑end delivery of missile integration programs for 4th and advanced 5th generation fighter aircraft. This role drives cross‑functional teams—including systems engineering, software, test & evaluation, logistics, and contracting—to ensure timely, cost‑effective, and compliant fielding of our missile solutions. The incumbent will serve as the primary interface with the Air Force, Joint Program Offices, and key industry partners while maintaining rigorous adherence to schedule, budget, and performance baselines.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Manage the full program lifecycle from integration planning through flight testing, platform certification, and Initial Operational Capability (IOC).
- Plan and execute integration of tactical missiles across multiple aircraft platforms via multiple simultaneous contracts.
- Develop program scope, objectives, and success criteria; establish and maintain the integrated master schedule (IMS), risk/opportunity register, and cost baselines.
- Execute a comprehensive risk and opportunity management process to identify, assess, and mitigate technical, schedule, and cost risks.
- Serve as the primary liaison between DoD acquisition offices, aircraft OEMs, subsystem suppliers, and test ranges to plan and execute safe store separation, telemetry verification, and live‑fire flight tests.
- Lead major programmatic reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR) and ensure timely closure of action items.
- Own the program budget—authorizing expenditures, tracking forecasts, and achieving cost‑to‑complete and EVMS performance targets.
- Develop new business opportunities through long‑range strategic planning, capture planning, and development of proposals and business plans.
- Build and mentor a high‑performing, multidisciplinary team of program managers, engineers, logistics, and acquisition specialists.
- Prepare and present program status reports, risk assessments, and decision briefs to senior leadership and customers.

The selected candidate will also oversee technical and operational execution of missile‑to‑aircraft integration, including:
- Interface Control Documents (ICDs) for physical, electrical, and logical interfaces (internal and external carriage)
- Missile virtual model development and test
- Ground and flight test planning and execution
- Verification of system‑level integration requirements
- F‑35 Software‑in‑the‑Loop (SIL) missile simulator development and testing in the SIL lab
- Mission Planning integration and analysis support (e.g., wind tunnel, CFD, structural) for weapon carriage and safe separation
- Hardware‑in‑the‑loop (HIL) and flight‑test campaigns; approve test plans, data reviews, and deviation waivers.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
- Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline with 8+ years of aerospace/defense program management experience OR a Master’s (MS/MBA) with 6+ years of mentioned experience
- Proven expertise and experience with weapon‑to‑aircraft interfaces, store‑separation criteria, test‑and‑evaluation planning, and fighter‑aircraft avionics architectures.
- Experience leading programs to completion on schedule using program‑management tools such as Earned Value Management System (EVMS), Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), and Risk & Opportunity Management processes.
- Strategic thinker experienced in developing multi‑year aircraft integration roadmaps and long‑range program plans.
- Skilled decision‑maker in uncertain, high‑stakes environments.
- Strong communicator adept at negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and conflict resolution.
- Current U.S. Government DoW Secret clearance with ability to get a Sensitive Access Program (SAP) clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
- Experience in tactical missile integration on aircraft
- Experience with store separation testing, wind tunnel data, or avionics flight software
- Direct experience working with F-16 Configured Systems or F-35 Mission Systems
- Strong track record of executing Fixed price (FFP) contracts
- Strong knowledge of aircraft systems (structures, power‑distribution, flight controls, data buses)
- Familiarity with multi‑mode tactical missile subsystems (guidance, propulsion, warhead, launch hardware)

- Familiarity with Agile/DevOps practices for software‑intensive missile guidance or flight‑control code

We are seeking an exceptional Program Manager to lead Stage 1 of a new and emerging capability area for Northrop Grumman Australia, establishing the foundations for future growth and long-term success.

As the key interface between Defence, industry partners, international stakeholders and internal teams, you will play a pivotal role in driving integration, maintaining alignment of priorities, and ensuring successful delivery against program objectives.

Working closely with program leadership in the United States, you will oversee the integration and execution of Australian activities, ensuring local priorities, stakeholder expectations and delivery commitments are coordinated and achieved.

You will bring together multidisciplinary teams across engineering & technical, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, safety and support functions while fostering strong customer relationships and a culture of collaboration, accountability and delivery excellence.

Success in this role will be defined by your ability to influence without authority, build trusted partnerships, align diverse stakeholder groups, and bring people together around a shared outcome.

This role will suit a leader who thrives in emerging environments, enjoys building capability from the ground up, and is motivated by delivering outcomes through collaboration, influence and strong stakeholder engagement.

About You
You are an accomplished program leader with a track record of delivering complex programs while building high-performing teams and stakeholder relationships.
You will bring:
- Experience leading  complex programs within Defence, aerospace, manufacturing, engineering or similarly regulated industries

- Strong commercial and financial management capability

- Demonstrated success establishing, scaling or transforming programs and organisations

- Exceptional stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to apply values based leadership to influence and build credibility across customer, industry and internal stakeholder groups

- Experience leading multidisciplinary teams through complexity, growth and change

- Proven experience at building a proactive safety culture

- Strong risk management, governance and delivery expertise

- A strategic mindset combined with a passion for execution and results

- Experience within explosive ordnance, guided weapons, munitions, advanced manufacturing, or similar complex capability environments will be highly regarded

If you are a collaborative leader who enjoys bringing stakeholders together, driving integration across multiple organisations, and delivering outcomes in a complex and emerging environment, we encourage you to apply.

What we offer:
Whatever your role, life stage or background, you can shape your career here in your way with highly challenging work, great colleagues and career development, plus a range of flexible benefits and working patterns.

- Salary packaging including novated car leases and the option to purchase additional annual leave

- We offer all employees access to our Health & Wellbeing program and Employee Assistance program

- Employee Discount Program

- Employee Recognition Program

For more information or a confidential discussion, please contact Eve Mountney. Evelyn.mountney@au.ngc.com

RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems (NGMS) is looking for you to join our team as a  Principal Operations Program Management Specialist (Principal Production Operations) based in  Rolling Meadows, IL.   This role is full-time onsite.

The candidate will support production, development, business, and other processes in a team-based manufacturing environment. Performs activities in a variety of cross-functional areas including production planning and control, total quality management, systems, manufacturing, equipment and facilities engineering, material management, and process reengineering. The incumbent may facilitate self-directed work teams, provide training in core skill areas to teams and peers, and interact with internal and external customers with respect to product planning, problem resolution, and process improvement. Incumbents are generally experienced in one or more areas of manufacturing operations. This highly motivated individual will be responsible for providing objective-oriented direction to multifunctional teams, including Operations functional support organizations, to ensure all program and manufacturing goals and objectives are met.

What you will get to do:
- Serve as the primary Manufacturing Operations interface with the Program Office,

- Coordinate/collaborate with engineering, Supply Chain Management, and Mission Assurance on all aspects of manufacturing programs.

- Responsible for managing proposals, production planning, and execution of manufacturing programs, while monitoring and addressing all cost, schedule, performance, and quality issues.

- Represent the Operations Manufacturing organization as a prime contact on contracts or programs. Interact with senior internal and external personnel on significant matters often requiring coordination between organizations.

- Oversee the generation of proposals, including basis of estimates, resource codes, estimate rational, bid codes, and overhead and labor rates.

- Ability to develop and maintain Production tools/metrics regarding Microsoft Excel Macro functions.

- Responsible for the overall performance of the Operations Team's activities to assure compliance with company objectives and obligations.

- Monthly reconciliation of Sales Order WBS to MRP WBS for accuracy and consistency.

Basic Qualifications for the Principal Production Operations Specialist:
- Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 5 years of related work experience; OR a Master’s degree and 3 or more years of relevant work experience; OR 9 years relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.

- Experience leading teams or projects.

- Experience with Material Requirements Planning (MRP).

- Experience with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).

- Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret Clearance.

- US Citizenship required.

Preferred Qualifications for the Principal Production Operations Specialist :
- Experience with taking a prototype to full rate production

- Experience in the defense/aerospace industry

- Experience performing in a fast-paced manufacturing and development environment.

- In-depth experience with Manufacturing Resource Planning (MRP), production planning, and material management

- Experience with Earned Value reporting and analysis.

- Experience with all aspects of proposal generation

Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. The Engineering Program Manager (EPM) is responsible for leading end-to-end engineering execution across the full program lifecycle. The EPM ensures the integrated engineering team delivers on cost, schedule, and technical performance. This role works in close partnership with the Program Manager and Chief Engineer to drive program success and meet commitments. EPMs are essential to strengthening how we execute—bringing consistency, rigor, and visibility across all engineering efforts on a program.

Key Responsibilities:

- Lead engineering execution across the entire program lifecycle (capture through delivery)
- Drive cost, schedule, and technical performance with disciplined execution
- Integrate across all engineering functions and partner organizations (GSC, MFG, MA) to ensure cohesive program alignment
- Enable data-informed decisions using program metrics and performance indicators
- Ensure adherence and appropriate rigor to all engineering processes
- Partner with Program Managers and Chief Engineers to align technical scope, staffing, and execution plans
- Identify, communicate, and mitigate risks and issues early
- Drive milestone reviews (e.g., SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR) with clear entry/exit criteria and readiness

This position will be full-time, on-site at our Rolling Meadows, IL location.

This position is contingent upon funding/contract award, special access program, and acquiring and maintaining the necessary U.S. Government security clearance per customers' requirements prior to start.

Basic Qualifications:

- BS degree in Mechanical, Electrical Engineering, Physics or other STEM field with 12+ years of related experience, MS degree in STEM field with 10+ years of related experience, or PhD in STEM field with 8+ years of related experience
- 5+ years of related engineering experience working in an engineering organization at a defense contractor during EMD and/or LRIP phases
- Experience working collaboratively on complex projects that encompass hardware, software, and firmware
- Experience in development and Earned Value Management (EVM) of cost accounts and schedules
- U.S. Citizenship required
- Active U.S. Government Secret security clearance

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience using metrics to drive decisions and program outcomes
- Demonstrated strong written and verbal communication skills including presentation experience briefing senior levels of leadership, both internal and external
- 9+ years engineering experience, including 5+ years leading multi discipline engineering teams ​
- Experience in all aspects of the engineering process from proposal / requirements analysis through verification testing and fielding of systems
- Experience in a Systems Engineering Integration & Test environment from one or more of the following specialty areas: EOIR systems, sensors, optics, antenna design, direction finding, geolocation, threat analysis
- Experience decomposing requirements for DoD-based platforms or systems
- Demonstrated expertise in SysML modeling and MBSE tools (e.g., IBM Rational DOORS, Enterprise Architect, Cameo). Ability to develop and maintain system models, traceability matrices, and verification cross‑reference artifacts
- Strong understanding of engineering execution across the full program lifecycle (beyond task tracking or a single discipline)
- Proven ability to collaborate across functions, sites, and stakeholders
- Familiarity with Northrop Grumman processes and operating procedures
- CAM certification with experience in ETCs and CEACs (or demonstrated experience performing CAM responsibilities)
- Demonstrated success guiding teams through proposals and Basis of Estimate (BOE) generation, program planning including start-up, Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs), milestone or gate reviews and through all execution phases ​
- Active U.S. Government Top Secret security clearance

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is seeking a Staff Engineering Program Manager (EPM) in Woodland Hills, CA. This role will be a Deputy EPM role working directly with the EPM to lead engineering execution for the Sentinel Program with a strong emphasis on developing an inertial measurement system. You will partner closely with Program Managers, Chief Engineers, discipline functional engineering management, and other support organizations to deliver on cost, schedule, and technical commitments.
This is a full‑time, on‑site role in Woodland Hills, CA.

What You’ll Get To Do
The EPM is accountable for cost, schedule, and execution of all engineering scope on the program and ensures work is completed within approved budget and contractual boundaries across all IPTs.
Key Responsibilities
• Engineering execution across the full program lifecycle (capture through delivery) for airborne navigation systems.
• Ensure engineering execution meets the applicable level of rigor and aligns with standards including MIL‑STD‑810 for environmental qualification, DO‑178 and MIL‑STD‑882 for safety‑critical software development, and DO‑229 for GPS integrity certification.
• Serve as the primary engineering interface to the Program Manager, Chief Engineer, and functional organizations (Systems, Software, Hardware, Test, Manufacturing, Supply Chain).
• Develop, review, and defend engineering proposal estimates and BOEs.
• Oversee CAM responsibilities for engineering scope, rolling wave planning, budget allocation, Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) maintenance, earned value status, and estimating total costs to complete efforts.
• Support schedule and financial updates, lead engineering Page and Line (P&L) reviews, and drive data‑informed decisions using program metrics.
• Develop staffing plans and Work Load Forecasts (WLF) and partner with functional managers to project and secure resources.
• Proactively identify, communicate, and burn down program execution risk, driving risk/issue/opportunity handling plans across IPTs.
• Develop and execute risk mitigation plans and return‑to‑green plans for efforts on the program at risk of not meeting their baseline cost, schedule, or technical targets.
• Ensure adherence to Northrop Grumman and customer engineering processes, configuration management, and rigorous entry/exit criteria for major reviews (e.g., SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR).
Basic Qualifications – Staff EPM
• Bachelor’s degree in a STEM or related technical field with 12+ years of related experience; or Master’s with 10+ years; or PhD with 8+ years
• U.S. Citizenship.
• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Secret security clearance.
• Extensive experience leading multi‑disciplinary engineering teams and serving as an engineering leader (e.g., EPM or IPT Lead) on complex programs.
• Deep experience in systems development, integration, and test across the full lifecycle for complex electronic or avionics systems.
• Demonstrated experience with EVM, CAM responsibilities, and management of cost, schedule, and technical performance for engineering scope.
• Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate across functions, sites, and senior stakeholders.
• Demonstrated experience using metrics to drive program decisions and outcomes.
Preferred Qualifications
• Advanced degree in a STEM or related technical field.
• Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent
• Active U.S. Government Secret or Top Secret clearance.
• Working knowledge of DoD systems engineering standards and lifecycle processes.
• Prior experience as an EPM, IPT Lead, or similar engineering leadership role.
• CAM certification and experience with ETCs, CEACs, and IBRs.
• Familiarity with Northrop Grumman processes and demonstrated success through proposals, BOE generation, program start‑up, and major reviews.

Integrated Thermal Systems is the world leader in two phase thermal control for Space applications.  We have designed, manufactured, and tested thermal control components / systems for nearly every US based satellite launched in the last 30 years and many international programs.  The ITS team also designs, fabricates, and tests honeycomb composite spacecraft structural panels (many with integrated thermal and electrical components).  Our systems are currently supporting some of the nation’s most important national security missions along with more public missions such as Cygnus Space Station Cargo Re-Supply, Boeing Starliner, Artemis HALO, Direct TV, XM Radio, Broadband Internet, NASA Weather & Telescope Missions, Mars Rovers, Robotic On-Orbit Satellite Servicing, and many more!  There are very few places in the Space Industry that offer direct exposure to the breath of programs our business supports.

Northrop Grumman is seeking a Staff Engineering Program Manager (EPM) & System Engineering Integration and Test (SEIT) Lead to join Mission System’s Business Execution Engineering Organization. This position will be located in Chantilly, VA .

The Engineering Program Manager (EPM) / Systems Engineering and Integration Team (SEIT) Lead will provide integrated technical and program leadership for a USAF Electronic Warfare (EW) low‑rate initial production (LRIP) program. This role is responsible for planning and executing systems engineering activities, managing the engineering scope within cost and schedule constraints, and ensuring technical integration across a geographically dispersed, multi‑discipline team of approximately 10–20 engineers. The EPM/SEIT Lead will interface with Program Management, engineering homerooms, manufacturing, test, quality, Global Supply Chain, and the prime contractor to deliver a technically sound, producible, and mission‑effective EW hardware solution.

Primary responsibilities of a candidate will include:
- Serve as the engineering liaison between Program Management, Manufacturing, Operations, Global Supply Chain (GSC), Quality, Engineering Functional Management, and IPT Leads.

- Plan and execute systems engineering per the SEMP and program processes, including requirements development, interface control, configuration management, and V&V.

- Establish and maintain an executable technical plan and schedule integrated with the IMS that fulfills contract/SOW technical requirements and LRIP objectives.

- Serve as CAM for Systems Engineering, managing SE work packages within an EVMS framework (planning, status, variance analysis, and RTG/corrective actions).

- Lead planning, execution, and closeout of key technical reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, SVR), peer reviews, configuration audits, and test/ship reviews.

- Define, control, and verify interface requirements across RF, digital, mechanical, power, and software disciplines, ensuring vertical and horizontal integration across IPTs.

Description

At Northrop Grumman Australia, our work contributes to some of the nation's most important Defence capabilities. As part of the MQ-4C Triton program, you'll play a critical role in ensuring aircraft, tooling and equipment are available when and where they're needed to support operational success. This is an opportunity to lead a high-performing logistics team, influence continuous improvement initiatives, and make a tangible impact within a complex Defence environment.

Your role:
As Supply Operations Lead, you'll lead a team responsible for warehouse, inventory, distribution and tooling operations supporting the Triton program. You'll ensure critical assets are received, stored, maintained and delivered safely, efficiently and in compliance with Defence and regulatory requirements.

Working closely with Defence stakeholders, maintenance teams and suppliers, you'll drive operational excellence, develop your team, manage inventory performance, coordinate freight activities, and identify opportunities to improve logistics processes across the program.

Key responsibilities include:
- Leading and developing a team of warehousing professionals, including workforce planning, training, performance management and quality oversight.
- Managing inventory, stock accuracy, warehousing operations and distribution activities to support Triton maintenance and operational requirements.
- Overseeing receipt, storage, inspection, picking, packing and dispatch of aircraft and non-aircraft parts.
- Coordinating inbound and outbound freight movements and supporting complex logistics activities across multiple stakeholders.
- Managing tooling, ground support equipment (GSE) and calibration activities to ensure operational readiness.
- Maintaining compliance with Defence, export control, warehousing and safety requirements, including ITAR obligations.
- Driving governance, reporting and continuous improvement initiatives across warehousing and distribution functions.
- Building strong relationships with Defence personnel, suppliers, freight partners and internal program teams to achieve operational outcomes.

About you:
You're a people-focused logistics professional who enjoys leading teams, solving complex operational challenges and delivering exceptional customer outcomes. You thrive in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment and bring a strong understanding of warehousing, inventory management and supply chain operations.

You'll bring:
- Experience leading warehousing, logistics or supply chain operations, ideally within Defence, aviation or a similarly regulated industry.
- Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate and develop high-performing teams.
- Experience managing inventory, distribution and warehouse compliance activities.
- The ability to build trusted relationships with Defence, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Knowledge of Defence logistics systems such as MILIS and CAMM2.
- Strong communication, problem-solving and continuous improvement skills.
- Ability to obtain and maintain an ADF NV1 Security Clearance.
- Dangerous Cargo Handling Certification (desirable).
- Current Forklift Licence (desirable).

Join a team where your expertise helps sustain a critical Defence capability, your ideas are valued, and your professional growth is supported. At Northrop Grumman Australia, you'll be empowered to solve complex challenges, collaborate with talented professionals and contribute to work that protects Australia's future.

What we offer:
Whatever your role, life stage or background, you can shape your career here in your way with highly challenging work, great colleagues and career development, plus a range of flexible benefits and working patterns.
- Professional development – further education, leadership development, professional industry memberships and unlimited access to a range of online training
- Salary packaging including novated car leases and the option to purchase additional annual leave
- Flexible working options, including hybrid working, 9 day fortnights, volunteer leave and varying start and finish times to suit your family needs
- 18 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid reservist leave
- We offer all employees access to our Health & Wellbeing program and Employee Assistance program
- Employee Discount Program
- Employee Recognition Program

For more information or a confidential discussion, please contact hayley.bincalar@au.ngc.com

As a Defence security clearance is required for this role, you must be an Australian Citizen. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) are applicable, as such your nationality may be a factor in determining your suitability for this role. You will also need to satisfy police checks and employment screening verification

Northrop Grumman Space Systems is seeking a highly qualified and energetic leader for the position of Manager 1 Supply Chain Programs to join our team in Dulles, VA.

This is an onsite position.  No relocation will be provided. This position’s standard work schedule is a 9/80. The 9/80 schedule allows employees who work a nine-hour day Monday through Thursday to take every other Friday off.

This individual will be responsible and accountable for the planning and execution of the supply chain strategy for all material and services content for a Program or portfolio of Programs.

Key responsibilities include program planning (i.e. developing a procurement plan for subcontracts and material while aligning Global Supply Chain (GSC) resources to meet that plan), supply chain metrics (i.e. on-time to place, on-time to need), supplier performance (i.e. line of balance, material status, supplier risk/opportunity management), and financial management (i.e. budget, sales forecasting of subcontract milestones and material).

The GSC PM will lead teams to ensure the placement and receipt of all material requirements support the program plan.  If anything falls off plan, the GSC PM will be responsible to steer resources to address as appropriate. Acts as the main focal point for the Program Management Office (PMO) for the entire supply chain and coordinates cross-functionally to ensure that all supply chain commitments are met, and that appropriate mitigation plans are developed and executed to address any programmatic risks related to suppliers. Briefs the PMO and executive management on the status and issues affecting Program cost and schedule performance.

Additional duties:

Program Supply Chain Execution & Subcontract Management
- Execute end-to-end material strategy and supply chain plans for assigned Development and Production Programs, aligning supply resources with customer requirements, corporate objectives, and product-line priorities
- Serve as the primary supply chain focal point for assigned Program Management Offices (PMOs), ensuring all supply chain commitments are met through proactive coordination across Subcontracts, Procurement, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Manufacturing, Contracts, and Operations
- Monitor and manage subcontract execution by tracking performance against Statement of Work (SOW) requirements, deliverable milestones, cost/schedule baselines, and compliance with contractual terms and conditions
- Develop and execute risk mitigation plans to address programmatic challenges related to supplier performance, material availability, lead time variability, and supply chain disruptions
- Manage financial forecasting and cost tracking for material purchases and subcontract obligations, coordinating with Finance and Business Management to align supplier invoice accruals and material delivery schedules with prime contract milestones, Estimate at Completion (EAC) projections, and program funding profiles to ensure accurate financial reporting and cash flow management
- Provide technical and analytical support to subcontract negotiations by developing should-cost models, conducting price/cost analysis, benchmarking supplier pricing against market rates, and identifying cost reduction opportunities without compromising quality or schedule performance

Supplier Performance Management & Quality Oversight
- Manage supplier performance by tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) including on-time delivery (OTD), quality metrics (First-Pass Yield, defect rates, non-conformances), cost performance, and compliance with AS9100/NADCAP standards and ITAR/EAR requirements
- Conduct supplier business reviews (weekly/monthly/quarterly) to analyze supplier progression, delivery performance, spend patterns, and continuous improvement initiatives; prepare executive-level supplier performance reports and scorecards
- Support supplier corrective action processes by coordinating with Quality on Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs), monitoring containment actions, verifying root cause analysis, and tracking closure of corrective and preventive actions (CAPA)

Engineering Qualification & Product Lifecycle Management
- Manage qualification subcontracts for new product introductions and supplier qualifications, partnering closely with Engineering to coordinate design reviews, qualification testing requirements, and technical assessments while ensuring Subcontract Data Requirements Lists (SDRLs) deliverables—including test plans, test reports, design data packages, and certification documentation—are tracked, reviewed, and submitted on schedule
- Oversee engineering-intensive qualification efforts by coordinating between suppliers, Engineering, Quality, and Mission Assurance during First Article Inspections (FAI), environmental testing, structural testing, performance validation, and reliability qualification cycles to ensure all technical requirements and acceptance criteria are met
- Conduct make-vs-buy analyses and provide strategic recommendations based on total cost of ownership, supplier technical capabilities, qualification risk assessments, capacity constraints, and sourcing considerations for development and production programs
- Manage product lifecycle transitions including phase-in/phase-out activities, manufacturing ramp-up/ramp-down following successful qualification, and end-of-life (EOL) material planning in coordination with Sourcing, Operations, Finance, and Engineering

Proposal & Business Acquisition Support
- Develop comprehensive supply chain strategies for proposal activities, including Basis of Estimates (BOEs), material forecasts, supplier identification, make/buy plans, risk assessments, and procurement strategies for new business opportunities
- Participate in Business Acquisition Process (BAP) activities and gate reviews, ensuring proposed program plans have complete and accurate schedules, budgets, resource plans, and subcontracting strategies that are executable and competitive
- Provide rapid-response proposal support for quick-turn capture efforts, including competitive cost analysis, teaming arrangements, and supplier capability assessments

Strategic Planning, Reporting & Program Controls
- Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings on supply chain performance, supplier scorecards, program risks, mitigation strategies, and cost/schedule impacts to senior leadership and Program Directors during Program Management Reviews (PMRs)
- Develop data-driven insights and analytics using ERP, Cognos, and business intelligence tools to identify trends, support decision-making, and recommend process improvements that enhance supply chain efficiency and reduce costs
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives by championing Lean/Six Sigma methodologies, process optimization, and best-in-class procurement practices to increase operational excellence

Basic Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree
- Minimum 6 years of supply chain, program management, procurement, purchasing or closely related experience
- At least 2 years of lead or supervisory experience
- Knowledge of general procurement and subcontract execution workflows
- Understanding of general manufacturing and purchasing workflows
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel
- Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance

Preferred Qualifications:
- Currently holds an active SCI security clearance
- Experience in the Aerospace/Defense/Space industry
- Understanding of forecasting and planning with an emphasis on driving execution to need with an emphasis on working knowledge of Integrated Master Schedules
- Experience working with multiple complex contracting types and agreements, including Firm Fixed Price and Cost Reimbursable, and possess knowledge relating to special payment provisions (progress of performance base payments).
- In-depth experience with proposal process, pricing instructions, terms and conditions and evaluating the adequacy of subcontractor proposals received.

As one of the largest global security companies in the world, Northrop Grumman is proud to help our nation’s military personnel navigate their next chapter into civilian careers. Approximately 20% of Northrop Grumman’s 100,000 employees self-identify as veterans, and more than 2,000 are reservists.

The Northrop Grumman SkillBridge Program is an approved SkillBridge Program under Dept. of Defense Instruction 1322.29. The program is an opportunity for service members preparing for civilian careers to gain valuable civilian work experience during their last 6 months of service, for up to 180 days. The  SkillBridge Program is open to all ranks and experience levels. SkillBridge participants are not eligible for compensation from Northrop Grumman, as they continue to receive military compensation and benefits as active-duty service members .

Responsibilities for SkillBridge Program participation are:

Northrop Grumman Corporation (NGC) has developed the Northrop Grumman –  SkillBridge Program (SkillBridge) utilizing the DoDI guidance for SkillBridge.  Through this program, the service-member will work on site with their host company, gaining experience in an entry to mid-level career path. The service member will be on the job training supporting a work schedule equivalent to 40hrs per week. Outlined below are the Goals, Objectives, and Outcomes for the program.
Goals – Provide separating service-members with job skills training in a professional setting during the final phase of their military service. This program is specifically designed to offer hands-on experience that result in the potential to convert to a full-time opportunity as the conclusion of the training.  Participants will serve as a pipeline for high-speed, motivated military candidates into NGC.
Objectives - Service Members who complete the SkillBridge program will be highly trained, capable, future employees that align to the specific needs of the organization and are prepared to meet the NG mission “Defining Possible” on Day 1. This program provides comprehensive hands-on experience including professional development, networking with leadership, and training specifically focused on NG leadership principles, company history, customer/stakeholder engagement, product and service overview, and core job responsibilities.
Outcome – Offer service-members preparing for civilian careers a rewarding opportunity to join the Northrop Grumman team.

SkillBridge Eligibility:

- Has served at least 180 days on active duty

- Is within 12 months of separation or retirement

- Will receive an honorable discharge

- Has taken any service TAPS/TGPS

- Has attended or participated in an ethics brief within the last 12 months

- Received Unit Commander (first O-4/Field Grade commander in chain of command) written authorization and approval to participate in SkillBridge Program prior to start of internship.
